# Find the inference bottleneck first: weights, KV content, or cache tiers

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/foundation-models/compression-and-cache.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-26 · 43 topic entries / 20 representative comparisons

AWQ reduces weight bit width; GQA shares KV heads; DropKV and TwinKV change retained content; KVMEM manages executable history views; Remote KV Tiers decides cross-tier loading. They can combine, but one compression ratio cannot explain quality, recoverability, and end-to-end speed. FoldBias makes compressed caches compatible with standard interfaces by folding static bias into equal-width keys, while future query drift still causes error.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Four kinds of capacity reductions

AWQ stores the same weights in fewer bytes, GQA lowers KV heads per token, DropKV removes positions, and TwinKV reallocates a fixed position budget. The first two need not reduce history length and the latter two do not compress weights. AWQ can free room without changing long-output KV growth, while eviction may not fix weight-read bottlenecks.

Sources: [AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration](../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en.md) · [GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints](../../../../reproductions/2305.13245-gqa/README-en.md) · [DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en.md) · [TwinKV: A Composable Repair Pass for KV Cache Eviction via Pairwise Key Redundancy](../../../../reproductions/2608.27128-twinkv/README-en.md)

### Deletion versus movement changes future access

DropKV and TwinKV constrain visible history to what is retained. KVMEM separates the large address space from the small execution view; unselected blocks can remain in backing storage. Remote KV Tiers asks whether fixed load overhead plus bytes divided by bandwidth beats recomputation. Hits, retained data, GPU memory, and speed are distinct evidence. Local KVMEM keeps full backing cache and no remote implementation was measured.

Sources: [DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en.md) · [KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU](../../../../reproductions/2609.04852-kvmem/README-en.md) · [When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill](../../../../foundation-models/2610.21500-remote-kv-tiers/README-en.md)

### October 29: new methods and scope changes

ResCom adds a low-rank branch to a fixed quantized host to read activation rounding residuals; calibration and intercept must match that host. HOPE uses Gaussian–ReLU/Hilbert proxies to prune structured neurons and compensate downstream means. These are not universally equivalent pruning/quantization combinations. Local exact small components do not reproduce LLM or ImageNet matrices.

Sources: [AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration](../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en.md) · [ResCom: Activation Residual Compensation for Large Language Model Quantization](../../../../foundation-models/2610.35955-rescom/README-en.md) · [Hilbert Operator for Progressive Encoding (HOPE): A Mathematical Framework for Deconstructing Learned Representations in Deep Networks](../../../../foundation-models/2607.21366-hope-hilbert/README-en.md)

### Standard cache compatibility does not eliminate compression error

GQA changes per-token KV storage by sharing heads. FoldBias preserves head width and query paths while folding an existing compression's static logit bias into `β(q·u)`, accurate only when query projection is near one. Refit values after key rounding to match actual kernel inputs. AM key selection, NNLS, and engine integration remain independent; small matrices do not prove throughput or full cache quality.

Sources: [Folding Attention Biases into Keys Makes Compacted KV Caches Run on Standard Kernels](../../../../foundation-models/2610.36520-fold-bias/README-en.md) · [GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints](../../../../reproductions/2305.13245-gqa/README-en.md)

### Critical dependencies can be rearranged without reducing data volume

GQA reduces KV heads per position, while KVMEM controls when historical blocks enter the execution view. MLI does not aim to reduce KV bytes: it separates selection production and consumption across full layers, overlapping same-token indexing with main computation. The lookback counts full layers that retain indexers, not physical layer numbers; initial layers lacking predecessors keep the standard schedule. Concurrent execution must also wait on events at the first consumer and hold inputs and outputs until the join, or even a correct logical dependency graph can read unfinished results or reused memory. This is not caching old selections across tokens. A CPU dependency simulation or ordinary synchronous CUDA forward pass cannot establish the paper's overlap. This repository provides review only: the costly full experiment is not reproduced, with no local runtime or throughput evidence.

Sources: [GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints](../../../../reproductions/2305.13245-gqa/README-en.md) · [KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU](../../../../reproductions/2609.04852-kvmem/README-en.md) · [Multi-layer Indexer: Overlapping Selection and Attention in DeepSeek Sparse Attention](../../../../foundation-models/2611.03768-multi-layer-indexer/README-en.md)

### Input bytes, intermediate writeback, and scheduling overlap are distinct

AWQ uses activation-aware scaling to protect low-bit model weights. PiPNN II quantizes external graph points and maintains the best K after scaling each candidate, avoiding full distance-matrix writeback. MLI instead restructures critical same-token selection dependencies across layers, without targeting byte compression. Verify these separately through weight error, graph-build recall and time, and actual serving-stream overlap. Agreement with a full sort on a small matrix establishes PiPNN's local scoring semantics, not large-graph recall or kernel performance.

Sources: [AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration](../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en.md) · [Turbocharging PiPNN for Proximity and k-NN Graph Building](../../../../foundation-models/2611.05690-pipnn-ii/README-en.md) · [Multi-layer Indexer: Overlapping Selection and Attention in DeepSeek Sparse Attention](../../../../foundation-models/2611.03768-multi-layer-indexer/README-en.md)

### Distinguish the compressed object, writes, and random reads

AWQ changes model weights, using calibration activations to choose equivalent scaling before low-bit reconstruction. PiPNN II fuses quantized scoring with top-K during graph construction to avoid writing a candidate score matrix. GINGER searches an existing graph and reduces vector read bandwidth while scanning candidates. Their respective checks are output error from quantized weights, construction time and graph recall, and query throughput at fixed recall. Synthetic NTQ error does not replace the two system measurements.

Sources: [GINGER: Spicing Up Graph-Based Vector Search](../../../../foundation-models/2611.08306-ginger/README-en.md) · [Turbocharging PiPNN for Proximity and k-NN Graph Building](../../../../foundation-models/2611.05690-pipnn-ii/README-en.md) · [AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration](../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en.md)

### Spool: affine summaries for sliding recurrent windows

DropKV selects attention KV entries for eviction. Spool reconstructs shared recurrent state after expiry. Layerwise recorded-input exactness does not establish full-network equivalence. Storing D=A-I protects small deviations from identity in low precision. Composition is noncommutative. Exactness holds for recorded inputs within a layer, not whole-network recomputation: higher-layer cached features can retain expired-frame influence.

Sources: [Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.23228-spool/README-en.md) · [DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en.md)

### EchoMoE: compressed changes around cached reference states

MoEZip protects routing-sensitive KV entries. EchoMoE compresses expert-parallel activation communication. Their different storage/traffic targets make compression ratios incomparable as throughput evidence. Folding is algebraically equivalent to the compressed model, not lossless recovery of the original backbone. The paper also uses projection-weighted initialization followed by KL distillation and next-token adaptation. Analytic bytes are not measured RDMA traffic.

Sources: [Communicate the Change: Efficient Expert Parallelism via Activation Compression](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22215-echomoe/README-en.md) · [MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30206-moezip/README-en.md)

### RISA: recoverable storage and reusable sparse addresses

DropKV evicts KV to reduce storage. RISA limits recurring reads while retaining COLD for recovery. Read and storage budgets cannot be exchanged as memory/latency conclusions. The maximum is taken after two complete dot products, not the coordinate-wise QUEST bound. Later steps reuse addresses, not attention outputs, and recompute one softmax with current queries/KV. Exact storage does not imply dense-equivalent decoding.

Sources: [RISA: Recoverable Sparse Attention for Block-Diffusion Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22191-risa/README-en.md) · [DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en.md)

### Protecting quantization-sensitive content is not verifying deployment execution

The reviewed AWQ README uses XW=(XS^-1)(SW) and activation-driven scaling to reduce quantized output error. Its local implementation omits TinyChat kernels, so MSE is not end-to-end throughput. Beyond Bitwidth checks fused-module weight types, activation policies, kernels and fallbacks, then validates service gates on an independent final set. Restoration gains are nonadditive, and activation precision changes jointly with INT8 protection; allocation alone is not isolated. A100 numerical simulation cannot verify native B200 NVFP4 execution.

Sources: [Beyond Bitwidth: Deployment-Constrained Mixed-Precision Quantization for Multilingual LLM Inference on NVIDIA Blackwell](../../../../foundation-models/2611.21974-beyond-bitwidth/README-en.md) · [AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration](../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en.md)

### LoopCache: Accelerating Long-Context Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers

Spool reconstructs recurrent state for fixed recorded layer inputs. LoopCache schedules loop-specific KV reads and corrects approximate speculation through an exact branch. Their exactness claims concern different objects. Equality at the margin threshold triggers replacement. Future-loop harmful-switch labels are analysis only, never runtime oracles. Approximate speculative-cache computation cannot commit a token; the exact branch is mandatory.

Sources: [LoopCache: Accelerating Long-Context Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers](../../../../foundation-models/2611.24301-loopcache-interface/README-en.md) · [Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.23228-spool/README-en.md)

### FrontierReplay: Split-Free Exact Prefix Caching for Hybrid Language Models

ReplaySSM reduces per-token matrix-state writes during decoding/speculation through input caching, output-only reads and acceptance rollback. FrontierReplay instead materializes exact checkpoints at structural boundaries for subsequent prefill and decides which states remain useful. Periodic refresh and split-precision anchors are not conversation-frontier retention. Existing standalone Triton evidence for local ReplaySSM cannot certify this host-policy component; the two input logs are not interchangeable. Section4.3 uses16-token pages. Native chunk ends must already be16-aligned: silently rounding them down would invent an exposed state. Completed turns may use the last page passed during decode, while structural targets may be rounded down and still require replay. Branch depths are at least256, and the replay window is1024tokens. Missing live anchors or log pages force an exact cut. Falcon-H1 never saves/restores below1568tokens. Section4.4 tiers are dead−1, superseded0, natural1, unused template/turn2, proven3 and running4. Repeated restores by one request do not prove reuse. A checkpoint becomes visible only after completion; failed or pending states cannot hit, and leases protect in-use anchors. Long-prefix protection selects the deepest natural checkpoint within one prefill budget before the stable end, at depth at least4096.

Sources: [FrontierReplay: Split-Free Exact Prefix Caching for Hybrid Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.26020-frontier-replay/README-en.md) · [ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State](../../../../reproductions/2610.13778-replayssm/README-en.md)

### DuoMI: Dual Mutual Information Regularization for Expert Reuse in Looped Transformers

EchoMoE reuses activation references and compresses communication deltas; DuoMI shares expert parameters and regularizes routing. A reference is not an expert pool. Communication reduction and routing reuse are different benefits, and tensor gradients establish no language-model gain. Each group has eight sequences. Apply thresholds per group and pool before averaging. Defaults:tau=1,g_max=.02bits,D-band[.05,.30]bits,and weights.1. Soft D is not the Top-k replacement fraction; D=1-retention holds only for uniform hard Top-k distributions. The language, load-balancing and z-loss objectives retain their baseline coefficients.

Sources: [DuoMI: Dual Mutual Information Regularization for Expert Reuse in Looped Transformers](../../../../foundation-models/2611.33952-duomi/README-en.md) · [Communicate the Change: Efficient Expert Parallelism via Activation Compression](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22215-echomoe/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Which memory growth terms do AWQ and GQA change in long conversations, and why might eviction still be needed? {#cross-weights-versus-history}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** AWQ lowers resident weight bytes. GQA lowers per-token KV bytes but history count still grows. DropKV-like selection can bound history count while risking information loss. Report the three quantities separately.

    **Illustrative example:** Thinner shelves do not reduce the arrival of books; GQA makes books smaller and eviction decides which books stay.

    Sources: [AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration](../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en.md) · [GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints](../../../../reproductions/2305.13245-gqa/README-en.md) · [DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en.md)

### How do DropKV and TwinKV differ when two important KV entries are redundant? {#cross-importance-versus-substitution}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** DropKV estimates each entry's output impact from observed attention probabilities and values. TwinKV repairs a base set by swapping donors with substitutes for orphans without alternatives. They address individual importance and set coverage and can combine, but require quality and budget checks.

    **Illustrative example:** Two near-duplicate plan entries can be exchanged to recover the only authorization scope if key similarity really implies substitutability.

    Sources: [DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en.md) · [TwinKV: A Composable Repair Pass for KV Cache Eviction via Pairwise Key Redundancy](../../../../reproductions/2608.27128-twinkv/README-en.md)

### Why might Remote KV Tiers recommend recomputation after KVMEM finds a block? {#cross-cache-hit-versus-recompute}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** An address makes reuse possible, not free. Low bandwidth, small blocks, or queueing can make `T0 + bytes/bandwidth` exceed a new prefill. Execution view limits visibility; the break-even rule decides how to retrieve. Hit rate alone cannot choose.

    **Illustrative example:** A remote hit on a short prefix may lose to local recomputation, while a long prefix amortizes fixed overhead.

    Sources: [KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU](../../../../reproductions/2609.04852-kvmem/README-en.md) · [When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill](../../../../foundation-models/2610.21500-remote-kv-tiers/README-en.md)

### Why can't ResCom correction rank be read as the number of HOPE neurons that can be pruned? {#cross-oct29-method-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** ResCom budgets low-rank output-error compensation. HOPE costs depend on neuron Hilbert capacity and original parameter footprint. Their parameter locations, states, and calibration assumptions differ.

    **Illustrative example:** Keeping every quantized output plus a rank-two correction is not deleting two neurons and compensating the downstream mean.

    Sources: [AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration](../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en.md) · [ResCom: Activation Residual Compensation for Large Language Model Quantization](../../../../foundation-models/2610.35955-rescom/README-en.md) · [Hilbert Operator for Progressive Encoding (HOPE): A Mathematical Framework for Deconstructing Learned Representations in Deep Networks](../../../../foundation-models/2607.21366-hope-hilbert/README-en.md)

### Why check future query quality when FoldBias preserves head width and works with a standard kernel? {#cross-fold-bias-compatibility-not-universal-equivalence}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Folded bias is `β(q·u)`, not always β. The mean constraint `μ·u=1` only fits the context distribution; future queries can drift. GQA head sharing compresses another object. Verify compatibility, memory, and quality separately.

    **Illustrative example:** With a future projection of 0.6, only about 60% of the original bias remains despite valid tensor shapes.

    Sources: [Folding Attention Biases into Keys Makes Compacted KV Caches Run on Standard Kernels](../../../../foundation-models/2610.36520-fold-bias/README-en.md) · [GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints](../../../../reproductions/2305.13245-gqa/README-en.md)

### Why is MLI consuming an earlier layer's selection different from KVMEM retrieving an old block or reusing a previous generated token's selection? {#cross-nov04b-overlap-not-kv-compression}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** MLI moves the consumer of a selection within the same token; that token's indexer still computes a fresh selection, creating an overlap window across full layers. KVMEM retrieves historical KV blocks and materializes them in a bounded execution view. A previous token's selection may no longer suit the current query, so cross-token reuse cannot substitute for MLI. Real overlap also requires event waits, tensor lifetimes and actual serving kernels. Local status is review-only, not a CPU simulation advertised as an implementation.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Reading top-k freshly computed for the current token by an earlier full layer rearranges dependencies. Taking top-k left by the previous generated token changes selection freshness. Similar-looking forms of reuse are not the same algorithm.

    Sources: [Multi-layer Indexer: Overlapping Selection and Attention in DeepSeek Sparse Attention](../../../../foundation-models/2611.03768-multi-layer-indexer/README-en.md) · [KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU](../../../../reproductions/2609.04852-kvmem/README-en.md)

### Both PiPNN II and MLI change how steps are organized. Why can't both be explained as eliminating an intermediate tensor? {#cross-nov06-score-fusion-versus-scheduling}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** PiPNN II scores each candidate and updates top-K without materializing all distances; row scales must be applied first. MLI still computes fresh selections but lets a later full layer consume a previous selection, enabling same-token index work to overlap main computation. One changes materialization and the other changes dependency and overlap. CPU agreement with a full sort cannot establish GPU overlap.

    **Illustrative example:** Example: Keeping only three distances out of 100 scores checks that full-table writeback is unnecessary and the result matches. Whether two CUDA streams advance together needs separate event and first-consumer measurements.

    Sources: [Turbocharging PiPNN for Proximity and k-NN Graph Building](../../../../foundation-models/2611.05690-pipnn-ii/README-en.md) · [Multi-layer Indexer: Overlapping Selection and Attention in DeepSeek Sparse Attention](../../../../foundation-models/2611.03768-multi-layer-indexer/README-en.md)

### If NTQ reads a few fewer bytes per candidate, does that directly show faster PiPNN II construction or higher GINGER production QPS? {#cross-ginger-versus-pipnn-evidence}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Fused scoring in PiPNN II is on the construction path; NTQ stream splitting is on the search path. Query performance also depends on graph adjacency, reranking volume, and hardware caches and must be timed at fixed recall. The local byte counts exclude scales and graph storage and are not a system memory figure.

    **Illustrative example:** In the 31-dimensional CPU example, navigation reads 16 coarse-code bytes and only the shortlist needs eight extra refinement bytes. This does not establish full-graph traffic or construction time.

    Sources: [GINGER: Spicing Up Graph-Based Vector Search](../../../../foundation-models/2611.08306-ginger/README-en.md) · [Turbocharging PiPNN for Proximity and k-NN Graph Building](../../../../foundation-models/2611.05690-pipnn-ii/README-en.md)

### How does its exactness differ from KV eviction? {#cross-nov18-spool}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** It exactly replays recorded layer transitions; DropKV estimates attention-output perturbations. Neither statement establishes full-backbone replay equivalence.

    **Illustrative example:** A cached higher-layer feature can already encode an expired frame.

    Sources: [Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.23228-spool/README-en.md) · [DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en.md)

### Can compression ratios be compared directly with MoEZip? {#cross-nov18-echomoe}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. KV row retention and expert-activation traffic have different denominators, reference overhead and quality errors.

    **Illustrative example:** Saving50% of KV storage does not imply saving50% of RDMA bytes.

    Sources: [Communicate the Change: Efficient Expert Parallelism via Activation Compression](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22215-echomoe/README-en.md) · [MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30206-moezip/README-en.md)

### Is its budget identical to DropKV eviction? {#cross-nov18-risa}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. RISA retains unselected COLD pages. Its eligible-HOT cap excludes protected, recovered-COLD and mandatory rows.

    **Illustrative example:** A512-page eligible cap does not bound total reads or total storage to512pages.

    Sources: [RISA: Recoverable Sparse Attention for Block-Diffusion Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22191-risa/README-en.md) · [DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en.md)

### Does lower AWQ output error satisfy Beyond Bitwidth deployment gates? {#cross-nov18-beyond-bitwidth}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Local MSE checks quantization approximation; deployment also requires native packed formats, activation policy, no fallback, memory/latency and independently evaluated service quality.

    **Illustrative example:** Lower W4 layer-output MSE does not establish native B200 execution or Korean quality retention for an8B model.

    Sources: [Beyond Bitwidth: Deployment-Constrained Mixed-Precision Quantization for Multilingual LLM Inference on NVIDIA Blackwell](../../../../foundation-models/2611.21974-beyond-bitwidth/README-en.md) · [AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration](../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en.md)

### Is this the same exactness as Spool? {#cross-nov19-loopcache-interface}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Spool replays transitions for fixed recorded inputs. Lossless token commitment in LoopCache also needs the correct full KV branch.

    **Illustrative example:** A correct schedule ID does not imply that target verification ran.

    Sources: [LoopCache: Accelerating Long-Context Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers](../../../../foundation-models/2611.24301-loopcache-interface/README-en.md) · [Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.23228-spool/README-en.md)

### Do FrontierReplay and ReplaySSM solve the same problem because both log inputs? {#cross-nov21-frontier-replay}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. ReplaySSM targets decode-state writes, output-only computation and speculative rollback; FrontierReplay targets checkpoint production and retention at prefill structural boundaries. Similar algebra does not share serving policies, precision contracts or evidence.

    **Illustrative example:** Illustration: a correct sixteen-step decode refresh does not prove that a next-turn template boundary was saved and remains reachable.

    Sources: [FrontierReplay: Split-Free Exact Prefix Caching for Hybrid Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.26020-frontier-replay/README-en.md) · [ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State](../../../../reproductions/2610.13778-replayssm/README-en.md)

### Is cross-layer reuse the same in DuoMI and EchoMoE? {#cross-nov26-duomi}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. DuoMI regulates shared-FFN routing; EchoMoE reuses activation references and compresses communication deltas.

    **Illustrative example:** Illustration:the same expert may process very different activations in two rounds, so expert retention cannot substitute for communication bytes.

    Sources: [DuoMI: Dual Mutual Information Regularization for Expert Reuse in Looped Transformers](../../../../foundation-models/2611.33952-duomi/README-en.md) · [Communicate the Change: Efficient Expert Parallelism via Activation Compression](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22215-echomoe/README-en.md)

## Update log {#updates}

Updates record new approaches, changed trade-offs, and follow-up evidence.

**2026-11-26** · EchoMoE reuses activation references and compresses communication deltas; DuoMI shares expert parameters and regularizes routing. A reference is not an expert pool. Communication reduction and routing reuse are different benefits, and tensor gradients establish no language-model gain. Complete matrices are terminally cost-deferred; L1 or review is not capability evidence.

Affected: [DuoMI: Dual Mutual Information Regularization for Expert Reuse in Looped Transformers](../../../../foundation-models/2611.33952-duomi/README-en.md) · [Communicate the Change: Efficient Expert Parallelism via Activation Compression](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22215-echomoe/README-en.md)

**2026-11-21** · ReplaySSM reduces per-token matrix-state writes during decoding/speculation through input caching, output-only reads and acceptance rollback. FrontierReplay instead materializes exact checkpoints at structural boundaries for subsequent prefill and decides which states remain useful. Periodic refresh and split-precision anchors are not conversation-frontier retention. Existing standalone Triton evidence for local ReplaySSM cannot certify this host-policy component; the two input logs are not interchangeable. Local component evidence remains separate from high-cost non-reproduction.

Affected: [FrontierReplay: Split-Free Exact Prefix Caching for Hybrid Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.26020-frontier-replay/README-en.md) · [ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State](../../../../reproductions/2610.13778-replayssm/README-en.md)

**2026-11-19** · Spool reconstructs recurrent state for fixed recorded layer inputs. LoopCache schedules loop-specific KV reads and corrects approximate speculation through an exact branch. Their exactness claims concern different objects. Local contracts and high-cost non-reproduction remain separate.

Affected: [LoopCache: Accelerating Long-Context Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers](../../../../foundation-models/2611.24301-loopcache-interface/README-en.md) · [Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.23228-spool/README-en.md)

**2026-11-18** · AWQ searches activation-aware equivalent channel scales before uniform low-bit weight-only quantization. Beyond Bitwidth studies native B200 formats, mixed-precision allocation and quality/memory/latency gates. Important-channel protection is not module-level format allocation, and a small AWQ output-MSE check is not Blackwell execution evidence. The existing same-topic representative README was read; the comparison does not change the algorithm or claim cross-paper reproduction results.

Affected: [Beyond Bitwidth: Deployment-Constrained Mixed-Precision Quantization for Multilingual LLM Inference on NVIDIA Blackwell](../../../../foundation-models/2611.21974-beyond-bitwidth/README-en.md) · [AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration](../../../../reproductions/2306.00978-awq/README-en.md)

**2026-11-18** · DropKV evicts KV to reduce storage. RISA limits recurring reads while retaining COLD for recovery. Read and storage budgets cannot be exchanged as memory/latency conclusions. Local boundaries and high-cost non-reproduction are recorded separately.

Affected: [RISA: Recoverable Sparse Attention for Block-Diffusion Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22191-risa/README-en.md) · [DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en.md)

**2026-11-18** · MoEZip protects routing-sensitive KV entries. EchoMoE compresses expert-parallel activation communication. Their different storage/traffic targets make compression ratios incomparable as throughput evidence. Local boundaries and high-cost non-reproduction are recorded separately.

Affected: [Communicate the Change: Efficient Expert Parallelism via Activation Compression](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22215-echomoe/README-en.md) · [MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30206-moezip/README-en.md)

**2026-11-18** · DropKV selects attention KV entries for eviction. Spool reconstructs shared recurrent state after expiry. Layerwise recorded-input exactness does not establish full-network equivalence. Local boundaries and high-cost non-reproduction are recorded separately.

Affected: [Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.23228-spool/README-en.md) · [DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction](../../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en.md)

**2026-11-09** · Added e-means to distinguish centroid training, graph construction, and query read bandwidth. Closing means can reduce the training objective under fixed assignments without guaranteeing lower held-out error or better retrieval performance.

Affected: [e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs)](../../../../foundation-models/2611.09501-e-means/README-en.md)

**2026-11-07** · Added GINGER's Nested TurboQuant and compared weight compression, construction writes, and query reads with AWQ and PiPNN II. Verified that the official PiPNN II repository linked by GINGER remains a placeholder; prior local evidence is unchanged.

**2026-11-06** · Add PiPNN II alongside AWQ and MLI to distinguish input bit width, intermediate score writeback, and critical dependencies. Note that ranking follows candidate scaling and that the local CPU semantic reference is not full graph-construction performance.

**2026-11-04** · Add MLI alongside GQA and KVMEM: it rearranges same-token selection dependencies across full layers, without compressing KV or reusing old-token selections. **2026-10-29** · ResCom adds low-rank activation-rounding residual correction to a fixed quantized host, with host-matched calibration and intercept.
